'''Maha Ashour-Abdalla''' ({{langx|ar|مها عاشور عبدالله}}, 1943 &ndash; May 1, 2016) was an [[List of Egyptian Americans|Egyptian-American]] physics and astronomy professor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sauress.com/alhayat/168533|title=علماء عرب - المصرية الأميركية مها عاشور ترى في الفوضى منقذاً للفيزياء المعاصرة|last=|first=|date=|website=سعورس|language=ar|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-03-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/1268212|title=نماذج نسائية مشرفة (1) {{!}} المصري اليوم|website=www.almasryalyoum.com|language=ar|access-date=2020-03-03}}</ref> She was named a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1986 and of the [[American Geophysical Union]] in 1993.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://newsroom.ucla.edu/stories/in-memoriam:-ucla-physics-professor-maha-ashour-abdalla|title=In memoriam: UCLA physics professor Maha Ashour-Abdalla|website=UCLA|language=en-US|access-date=2020-03-03}}</ref>

She was born '''Maha Ashour''' in [[Alexandria]] and completed a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] degree at [[Alexandria University]]. She received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the [[Imperial College London]] in 1971. She was subsequently employed at the [[Centre national d'études des télécommunications]] in France. Ashour-Abdalla next moved to [[Los Angeles]]; from 1976 to 1985, she was a researcher at the  Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA). In 1985, she became a professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at UCLA. In 1999, she founded and became first director of UCLA's Center for Digital Innovation.<ref name=":0" />

Ashour-Abdalla founded the Space Plasma Simulation Group at UCLA, which developed one of the first [[magnetohydrodynamic]] simulations of the [[solar wind]], [[magnetosphere]] and [[ionosphere]]. Her research was supported by grants from [[NASA]] and the [[National Science Foundation]]. She was the primary investigator from UCLA for NASA's [[Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission]]. She has been author or co-author of over 270 research articles published in [[peer review|peer-reviewed]] journals.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=bruin/>

In 1982, with colleagues from France and Japan, she organized the International School for Space Simulations, which holds annual symposiums every two to three years to educate young [[space science|space scientists]] on [[computer simulation]] techniques. Ashour-Abdalla has also been involved in developing educational programs for [[primary school|primary]], [[secondary school|secondary]] and college students.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://senate.universityofcalifornia.edu/in-memoriam/files/maha-ashour-abdalla.html|title=Maha Ashour-Abdalla|last=|first=|date=|website=University of California Academic Senate|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-03-03}}</ref>

She was named a fellow of the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] in 1984. She received the [[Outstanding Civilian Service Medal]] from the American army in 2004. In 2005, she received an award from the [[European Space Agency]] for her contributions to the exploration of [[geospace]] using [[Cluster (spacecraft)|Cluster]].<ref name=":0" />

She married Dr. Mohamed Abdalla; the couple had one daughter.<ref name=":0" />

She died of [[liver cancer]] at the age of 72.<ref name=bruin>{{cite web |url=http://dailybruin.com/2016/05/10/longtime-physics-and-astronomy-professor-maha-ashour-abdalla-dies-at-72/ |title=Longtime physics and astronomy professor Maha Ashour-Abdalla dies at 72 |work=Daily Bruin |date=May 10, 2016}}</ref>

A scholarship was established in her name to support women wishing to pursue graduate studies in [[space physics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://giving.agu.org/campaign/maha-ashour-abdalla-scholarship-space-physics-fund/ |title=Maha Ashour-Abdalla Scholarship in Space Physics Fund |work=Giving to AGU |publisher=American Geophysical Union}}</ref>
